html:
In 372 CE a monk named Sundo arrived in the Korean kingdom of Goguryeo with Buddhist images and scriptures. He was sent by Fu Jian, ruler of the Former Qin in northern China, and King Sosurim welcomed him. This is the traditional start of Korean Buddhism.

The other kingdoms of the Three Kingdoms followed:

  • Baekje received the faith in 384 from the Indian or Central Asian monk Marananta, who came from the Eastern Jin in southern China.
  • Silla resisted longer. It made Buddhism a state faith around 527, after the martyrdom of the court official Ichadon, whose blood, legend says, ran white.

Kings welcomed Buddhism because it gave their rule a universal religion and brought Chinese learning, writing and art. Temples and monasteries spread across the peninsula, and under Unified Silla Buddhist art reached a peak. From Baekje, Buddhism passed on to Japan in the 500s (Buddhism reaches Japan), completing its journey east from India via China.
